_: Acknowledged SKIPS inside the mutation sandbox (`swe/mutation.py::_copy_project`).
Read by `swe/sandboxevidence.py::check`, which every `baseline_check` run now
calls on its own junit report -- zero extra suite runs. Round 431 (SWE-loop D).
WHAT AN ENTRY MEANS. A round ran the suite in the sandbox, saw this node skip,
looked at WHY, and signed it. `reason_pin` is the exact skip message: if it
changes, the node is being skipped for a reason nobody adjudicated and the check
goes red (`pin_expired`), exactly as `state/known-escalated-diffs.json` treats a
moved blob. An acknowledgement is not a mute button with no expiry.
`class` -- `sandbox_only` means the COPY caused it (established by running the
suite both ways, `swe/copyparity.py run`); `both` means the live tree skips it
too, so it is not a copy defect but it IS still a test that did not contribute
to the mutation score. Both are signed here on purpose: a one-sided run cannot
tell them apart, and the honest question a one-sided run CAN answer is `is every
test the sandbox did not run signed off`.
`kills_mutants` -- can this test's absence change a mutant verdict? `false` needs
evidence, and the evidence is line coverage of the files the campaign mutates.
An entry with `true` is printed LOUDLY on every campaign and never goes quiet.
This file is NOT `state/known-pristine-skips.json`. That one models a test git
does not carry; this one models a test the COPY does not run. Different trees,
different ignore lists, deliberately different registries.
`suites[].node_floor` is the node count the entries were taken against. It fires
only when the sandbox collects FEWER nodes -- a conftest that stops collecting a
file when something it reads is absent exits 0, reports no skip and no failure,
and was invisible to everything in this repo before round 431. Adding tests
makes the floor stale-low (never a false positive); removing them is what it is
for.
